title: I Took the Handbell Table Checkout to the Director Who Camped My Numbered Set

parts.text: I stepped into table three at 7:06 p.m. and director Amos was already using my numbered set. The board said: NINETY MINUTES. BELLS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty, choir librarian, holding a clipboard that listed our rehearsal. Amos shrugged. "Directors are the table." I photographed the board, the booking, and his gloves on my bells. Then I asked for the table checkout. At 7:14 the choir desk pinged why Amos's gloves sat on our set. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The choir desk can see Amos's gloves on table three during our rehearsal.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered handbell set — Part 1/2
social.description: Handbell table, a director on my bells, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the gloves. Would you have asked for the table checkout?

parts.text: Amos called it damping until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the table still. The set went back to my numbered cases. Amos ran a slot of their own and told the next director atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: DIRECTORS ARE NOT THE TABLE. I keep our rehearsal on a labeled card. Amos brown-bags his gloves. The table finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Directors are not the table — Part 2/2
social.description: Table checkout, numbered set, and a second line on the board. Was damping ever our rehearsal?
